Have ice cream the way your grandparents had ice cream.

That's been the Citrano family's promise on Metropolitan Avenue since 1968 — in a parlor that's been scooping since 1925. Eighteen flavors made from scratch, homemade hot fudge, caramel and syrups, and whipped cream piled high. Nothing trendy. Nothing rushed. Just the real thing.

A century on one corner

The parlor time forgot — on purpose

1925
A soda fountain opens

An ice cream parlor begins serving at 105-29 Metropolitan Avenue — marble counter, tin ceiling, wooden booths. Much of what you see today is original.

1968
The Citrano family takes over

Giuseppe Citrano, an immigrant from Southern Italy, buys the shop and names it Eddie's. (There was no Eddie — Vito jokes his father figured an unhappy customer couldn't get mad at him.)

2000s
Vito & Angelina carry it on

The second generation keeps everything as it was: same recipes, same equipment, same mantra — “Have ice cream the way your grandparents had ice cream.”

Today
NYC's oldest ice cream parlor

Generations of Queens families mark birthdays, first dates and engagements here — some in the same booths their grandparents sat in.
